issues.description: The problem description (Part 2) requires a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) (including a milkVolume parameter and a specific return format with volume), but the UML, task list, and the solution implement messageOnMilk() with no parameters. This mismatch in the method parameter list for Milkable.messageOnMilk() will confuse students about the correct interface signature to implement and will lead to compilation/signature conflicts if students follow the Part 2 text or the UML inconsistently.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either (A) update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk() with no parameters and the corresponding return format (matching the UML and solution), or (B) change the template and solution to define Milkable.messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all implementing classes (Seal, Goat, etc.) and tests to accept the double parameter and include the volume in the returned string. Ensure the UML, task descriptions, template, and solution all use the same signature.

issues.description: The problem statement (Part 2) specifies a method messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) that includes a milkVolume parameter and expects a return string containing the volume. However, both the template code (Main.java) and the solution implement the Milkable interface with a parameterless method messageOnMilk():String. This signature mismatch (same conceptual method named differently with/without a parameter) creates confusion: students may implement the method with a double parameter (following the text) which will not match the template/expected implementation, causing compilation or test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signature across artifacts. Preferred fix: update the problem statement to require messageOnMilk():String (no parameter) and adjust the described return value to "[Animal Type] [name] is milked". Alternatively, if the intent is to include volume, change the template and solution to define messageOnMilk(double milkVolume) and update all calls (e.g., Main.java) to pass a volume value.
